background: Danske Bank is Denmark's largest bank, a Nordic universal bank funded by Danish and Nordic deposits and covered bonds, lending to households and companies across Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland, with the Estonian money-laundering case behind it.
synthesis: All three main agencies rate the bank, AA- on average and the weakest of them at A+, one on a positive outlook and two stable, after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is solid on CET1 of 17.0%, above the median of EU and Nordic banks, but leverage of 4.4% is in the bottom quarter, and liquidity is middling, with LCR of 162% above the median and NSFR of 122% just below it. The direction is down: since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has fallen 1.6 points, leverage 0.4 points and LCR 18 points. The newest flagged item, on 5 Oct 2026, is a regulatory-compliance piece, and the rest include a move to a positive outlook by one of the three and an upgrade to guidance.
